Dynamic dispatch needs the host-created type descriptor/vtable to be usable on the device; the specification does not say how polymorphic type information is made available there, so whether a conforming implementation must link this is not stated. Failure is a link-time missing runtime symbol.

Dynamic dispatch on device needs implementation support that the spec only constrains through the declare target rule, so a link failure is arguably permitted.

Reading B is right on legality. Nothing in the text says how a polymorphic type descriptor or dynamic dispatch is made available on the device, so whether a conforming implementation must link this is not stated.

The mapped objects are non-polymorphic. No restriction forbids class dummies or dynamic dispatch in declare target procedures, so the link failure on a runtime symbol is an implementation defect. Moderate doubt since the specification does not describe polymorphic dispatch support.

Reading A overstates legality: the only relevant rule is that all type-bound procedures accessed in a target region must appear in a declare target directive. Both readings agree. The concrete bindings sq_area, rect_area and area_of carry declare target, but the deferred binding has only an abstract interface that cannot.
